q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: WITH ValidBeers AS (SELECT beer FROM serves WHERE serves.bar IN (SELECT bar FROM frequents WHERE drinker LIKE 'B%') GROUP BY beer HAVING COUNT(bar) >= 2), BeerPrices AS (SELECT serves.beer, serves.price FROM serves FULL OUTER JOIN ValidBeers ON serves.beer = ValidBeers.beer) SELECT bp.beer, MAX(bp.price) - MIN(bp.price) AS price_gap, AVG(bp.price) AS avg_price FROM BeerPrices AS bp GROUP BY bp.beer ORDER BY bp.beer

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses a LEFT OUTER JOIN to find the minimum price of each beer at any bar, and then joins this with the serves table to find the bar where this minimum price is served. Q2, on the other hand, first identifies valid beers (beers served at least twice by bars where a drinker 'B%' frequents), and then calculates the price gap and average price for these beers across all bars where they are served.
counterexample_dsp: The difference between Q1 and Q2 can be observed when a beer is served at multiple bars with varying prices, and the minimum price of the beer is not the price at which it is served at the bar where the drinker 'B%' frequents.
